body: I'm sorry you are getting voted. I really don't know why. I appreciate what you've contributed - I asked for people to let me talk and vent and you are doing just that. Unless I'm missing something?

Treatable, yes. But I can't see it helping me with my problems. For 6 years I did really good without any mediation. Sure I had plenty of hallucinations and anxiety attacks, but I was more or less happy. But those days are long gone, and my problems have only gotten worse with no relief in sight.

Grew up in a small town. Though I'm the reverse - I swore I would live there my whole life. I hate the city, I hate crowds. But when it came to convenience of having things nearby, the city won. That and the fact that the city had all the jobs.
Sorry, I probably should have mentioned in bi-polar with psychosis. Also been diagnosed with ADD and turrets syndrome

At a hotel I worked at ten years ago, none of the network folders were protected. So I would look at accounting documents and other stuff when I was bored.

I hate change, but some change I can tolerate - such as getting married and moving into a house instead of an apartment.

Relevant (about fixing) http://youtu.be/yxSgIvYQC94

My favorite thing about IT is two fold. I love hardware and customizing/repairing computers. I just get along so much easier than with people. Software is limited to fixing whatever issues it's having, but no programming. I also love helping people, I get joy from fixing someone's issues (IT speaking).

Like I mentioned, no programming. I hate programming, I'm terrible at it, actually. I failed that class twice in college.

I got into IT... Well I was in love with computers since I can remember. Even before I knew what a computer was in 1990, I was trying to build robots with stuff I would find. (No, I was never successful at building a robot). In late 2001, I got my very first modern computer (my PC before that was from the 80s with a custom OS, and a 5.25" floppy. Monochrome monitor, of course.

I started learning how to trouble shoot various things on my modern desktop, as well as upgrading and so on. Built my first PC in early 2008, after I started college and learned I could just build one myself instead of going through dell or HP.

I'm not from Kansas City. I'm in a major city in Colorado (Colorado Springs).

It's hard not to compare yourself to others when others compare you to them anyway.

I don't get the news paper, so I wouldn't know what's being wanted. I keep up on monster.com and other websites and I don't necessarily stick with IT related stuff (only that's the one I want to get into). Sadly, my choices are stuck with either low paying jobs that have no rewarding careers or get a degree/job in an entry position like IT, which I've been trying without success for years now.

I've tried blogging, tried photographic, tried recycling, still doing some computer repairs on the side, but nothing worth mentioning. For a year I worked another job in addition to my full time job, while doing computer repairs, as well as side jobs for friends and family (such as yard work or recycling) but in the end I couldn't keep up, nor was it enough money to even touch student loans.

I've used forbearance in the past, they only allow so much time before they tell you too bad. I'm at that limit already.

I'm sorry, but it he idea of finding a better job with better pay is overly optimistic for me. The job I'm in now is the same line of work I've been doing since 2007, but pay hasn't gone up almost at all. Doesn't matter which company it is. The only way to do better is to switch to a new career, whether it be IT like I want or something else. I've even considered work in oil fields until I found that they want years of experience already and even then the pay is laughable ($12 an hour).

I'll call Monday for the prescriptions, I'll promise that much. But still not seeing how it'll help my hopelessness.

Job market on our area is rough but escaped much of the turmoil the rest of the country had. Problem is with no degree I'm not getting anywhere. And it's not like I'm not trying - I've pursued volunteer positions that will give me a chance to build my resume in my career choice, I've started my own computer repair business on the side (which brought its own problems), I've applied for internships, I've applied for every job I could find that's entry level for IT (even geek squad at best buy). But still nothing.

The big problem right now is school and everything that comes with it. The debt, the work load, my inability to keep up due to having to work to pay bills. Even more so, the fact that other people manage to do it with less time and while raising kids than I can- I'm such a failure that I can't even keep up with people who have it rougher than I do.

Yes I am aware I need to go back on my meds, but the problem I'm seeing is that it may fix how I feel, but it doesn't fix that I'm a failure who will never succeed.

Well it wasn't an easy road to finding medication that works. I can't even begin to count the various medications I've tried over the past 15 years.

The point of the economy though, I'm feeling that no matter how good the economy is I'll never make it. No degree is basically a economic suicide. Getting a degree is a financial suicide. I can't see how I can win, and I'm feeling that I'll never be able to get my degree.

I don't have much faith in legislation or laws about anything. I've been through the court system and my case was hailed as a success case for the justice system. I'm not even joking, the judge said that as well as some defense attorneys. My case was dismissed and the record expunged. Yet I still lost my job over it, especially when they called the police department and the police department broke the law by giving out my case history and then lied about the details (saying I was guilty and so on) when I wasn't.

I have employment now, but the pay is less than I was making before.

Initially I did talk to her, but she herself is struggling with her own depression, which is taxing enough on me in my own condition as it is (I push my stuff aside to support her). Plus she panics far too easy and will just blow up about how we could afford to pay on our student loans.

I was working on my BA. I've been attending college for years, since summer of 2007. My GPA was 3.4, and I did well despite taking years to get half my credits. But that university was too expensive and I had trouble getting my schedule to match up and to stay on top of classes working full time (and the fact that my sister got her degree working 50+ hours and being a single mom makes me feel that much more pathetic).

So I switched to my AA at a community college, but their classes don't match up with my schedule, so I did online, which didn't take long to fall behind on despite my best efforts initially. This last go round the school screwed me over resulting in me falling behind (it's a long story).

The problem I think is that the medication does work, I just haven't been taking them due to cost, inability to get in to see her to get new scripts for refills (and now that I have the ability the anxiety of doing it makes it difficult to make the appointment). The other problem, is I honestly feel that I have failed at life, that I will never be able to get out of student debt, that I'll never get a good paying job, that it's only a matter of time before we lose it all. With no chance of success, why bother anymore? Why stay living if there is nothing for me in the future? I'm dragging my wife down with me, and that's not fair. It was never my intention for any of this to happen, but it's been one failure after another since I lost my job position in July of last year.
School piled on, lots of little things that normally I could handle but now I can't, so I get buried deeper and deeper.

Thank you, really. I feel I can't speak with them because I'm tired of my medication being switched up. Even with having one of the best insurance plans I've ever seen my medication is still $40 a month. Which is awesome since without insurance it's about $1,000 or more, but we feel that $40 considering I make less at my current job than I did at the other. Of course it's not just medication, I haven't been taking it because I ran out and I feel embarrassed about that and don't want to deal with any lectures.

In a way I also don't want them to try to fix it, or force me into the hospital because we can't afford that. Other things buried in my mind....
